data.title: Adrenaline (epinephrine) injection
data.summary: VI Emergency drugs · Endogenous catecholamine; α and β adrenergic agonist
data.body:
_Injectables · VI Emergency drugs_

**Class:** Endogenous catecholamine; α and β adrenergic agonist

## Mechanism of action
- α1: vasoconstriction → raises BP, reduces mucosal oedema
- β1: increases heart rate and contractility
- β2: bronchodilation; also stabilises mast cells (less mediator release)

## Pharmacokinetics
- IM into the anterolateral thigh gives faster, higher peak levels than SC
- Onset within minutes; short action (5–10 min) — repeat dosing may be needed
- Concentrations: 1 mg/mL (1:1000) for IM; 0.1 mg/mL (1:10,000) for IV in cardiac arrest

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Anaphylaxis — the first-line, life-saving drug
- Cardiac arrest (IV/IO)
- Severe angioedema with airway involvement
- With local anaesthetics (1:100,000–1:200,000) to prolong action and reduce bleeding

## Dose & formulations
- Anaphylaxis: 0.01 mg/kg of 1 mg/mL (1:1000) IM in the anterolateral thigh — adult and child over 12 years 0.5 mg (0.5 mL); 6–12 years 0.3 mg; under 6 years 0.15 mg
- Repeat every 5 min if no improvement
- Refractory anaphylaxis: IV infusion by experienced staff only (never give 1:1000 IV bolus)
- Cardiac arrest: 1 mg IV (1:10,000) every 3–5 min
- Autoinjectors: 0.3 mg (adult), 0.15 mg (child) — prescribe for patients with previous anaphylaxis

## Adverse effects
- Tremor, palpitations, anxiety, pallor, headache
- Tachyarrhythmias, hypertension, myocardial ischaemia (mainly with IV use or overdose)
- Tissue necrosis with accidental injection into digits (rare) or extravasation

## Contraindications
- None in anaphylaxis — always give
- Caution with local anaesthetic use: uncontrolled hypertension, severe heart disease, hyperthyroidism, phaeochromocytoma

## Drug interactions
- β-blockers: anaphylaxis resistant to adrenaline → give glucagon 1–5 mg IV; non-selective β-blockers may cause severe hypertension
- Tricyclic antidepressants, MAO inhibitors, cocaine: exaggerated pressor effect
- Halothane: arrhythmias

## Monitoring
- BP, pulse, SpO₂, ECG; observe for at least 6–12 h after anaphylaxis (biphasic reaction)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Use without hesitation in anaphylaxis in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- Anaphylaxis: 0.5 mg (0.5 mL of 1:1000) IM in the thigh — repeat after 5 min
- Antihistamines and steroids are only add-ons
- Glucagon for patients on β-blockers
- Every dermatology procedure room should have adrenaline ready

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.58 (local anaesthetics) and anaphylaxis sections; Resuscitation Council / WAO anaphylaxis guidance. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
